author: Rory Robinson
title: LIV Golf stars told harsh reality after they ask PGA Tour about returning - NewsBreak
text:
By Rory Robinson ,
54 minutes ago Some of LIV Golf's biggest stars may face the prospect of being tourless by the end of the 2026 golf season, with the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund set to withdraw funding from the project.
Multiple players from the Saudi-backed circuit have reached out to the PGA Tour about a potential return behind the scenes. But it is claimed that internal responses suggest that the Tour will not be particularly welcoming to the majority of players who left the prestigious Tour for upfront money, PGA disruption, and an attempt to alter golf's ecosystem.
Instead of an open-door policy, LIV Golf stars were met with strict eligibility rules that leave the majority of the league with no clear pathway back. It comes after some players sounded out another potential alternative.
• LIV Golf tells Bryson DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson and Phil Mickelson crushing news
• LIV Golf star steps off course and immediately reacts to bombshell breaking news
Brooks Koepka remains the only player to successfully return to the PGA via its strict Returning Member Program.
According to Golf Digest , the PGA's response to LIV players didn't provide straightforward instructions. The Tour's return program featured a laundry list of benchmarks that only Koepka, Jon Rahm , Bryson DeChambeau , and Cameron Smith met.
Those conditions include being away from the Tour for at least two seasons, winning a Major between 2022 and 2025, paying fines, committing to making charitable donations, and more.
There was still no guarantee of acceptance back when the Tour's window of acceptance was open from Jan. 12 to Feb. 2. Smith, Rahm, and DeChambeau all passed on the opportunity .
That decision, in retrospect, comes after LIV’s future is suddenly under threat. Reports from Telegraph Sport indicated that captains and staff have already been informed that Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund is set to withdraw its financial backing at the end of the 2026 season.
The league has reportedly been losing tens of millions per month, leaving its long-term viability in serious doubt. The PIF has over $900 billion invested in its assets, and its latest financial strategy for 2026-2030 does not include sports , unlike in past years.
Out of LIV’s 57-player ecosystem, at least 48 have PGA Tour experience. Entire teams, including 4Aces GC led by Dustin Johnson, to HyFlyers GC captained by Phil Mickelson, are built on former PGA Tour mainstays.
Those players who decided to leave the Tour for guaranteed money and leverage are now facing a landscape where options are limited, windows to join other tours are closing, and the PGA Tour holds all the cards.
Even the idea of a fallback through the DP World Tour has surfaced, with players reportedly exploring alternative routes to stay competitive. Patrick Reed revealed his return to the PGA Tour after leaving LIV to play on the DP World Tour.
While uncertainty grows behind the scenes, the leaderboard continues to move. Rahm’s Legion XIII sits atop the standings, with Sergio Garcia’s Fireballs GC and Louis Oosthuizen’s Southern Guards GC chasing behind.
